answer: The most convincing defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals account age times consecutive honest epochs, verified by peers through a shared prism of signed interaction receipts. New identities start hollow, with near-zero weight, so a sybil fleet cannot fast-track relevance; even flawless behavior needs a long horizon of honest epochs before an account matters. Attacker cost is mostly time plus locked reputation: any fraud detected resets epochs to zero, erasing months of standing, so sockpuppets are pointless.
